## Dung beetle thermal tolerance under humidity stress

Humidity is known to affect and shape the physiological tolerances of species, particularly their thermal tolerance. However, it remains uncertain how changing humidity conditions might alter the physiological tolerance of insects. In this study, I examine the response of dung beetles' physiological tolerance (measured by CTmin & CTmax) to various levels of humidity stress.

Authors - Thilina S Nimalrathna, Akihiro Nakamura

Institute - Forest Canopy Ecology Group, Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences

## Import necessary data

## Normality check

```{r}

## Thermal tolerance between Sub tropical and tropical
## CTmax data

################################ thermal.df.both.CTmax.50 ################################

# Check the normality-CTmax
ggdensity(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp, 
          main = "Density plot of CTmax",
          xlab = "CTmax")  # looks right skewed
ggqqplot(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp)

hist(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp, main="Histogram of CTmax", xlab="", breaks=10) # left skewed
skewness(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp, na.rm = TRUE) #-0.9143051
shapiro.test(as.numeric(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp))#p= 0.0003323 not normal. Will transform

# Transform data to be normal
thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans<-sqrt(max((thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp)+1)-(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp))

# Check the normality-CTmax
ggdensity(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans, 
          main = "Density plot of CTmax transform",
          xlab = "CTmax")  # looks right skewed
ggqqplot(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans) # Looks normal

hist(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans, main="Histogram of CTmax.transformed", xlab="", breaks=10) # looks normal
skewness(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans, na.rm = TRUE) # 0.07559757
shapiro.test(as.numeric(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50$set_temp.trans)) #p=0.1357 normal.
```

### Create species summary data tables for analysis

```{r}
# species_temp  table summarizes CTmin and CTmax by species and treatment
# this will be used for some of our linear models later that need averages by species
species_temp <- 
  thermal.df.all %>%
  group_by(species, metric, humidity) %>%
  summarise(temp = mean(set_temp,na.rm=TRUE))

species_temp <- pivot_wider(species_temp, names_from=metric, values_from=temp) # make different columns for average ctmin and ctmax
species_temp$range = species_temp$CTmax - species_temp$CTmin # calculate range from CTmax to CTmin
species_temp
```

# Question 1: Analysis for CT differences between climatic regions

Question: How do dung beetle thermal tolerances respond in different climate zones?

Hypothesis 1: Beetles from the subtropics have lower CTmax and CTmin, but larger thermal tolerance range, because of higher temperature range in subtropics.

## Analysis for CTmax

### Sample summaries

```{r}

# MSP_06 - Synapsis birmanicus
# MSP_07 - Onthophagus sp.08		
# MSP_20	- Onthophagus sp.05

library(dplyr)

# CTmax
# 1. Total counts: number of unique species and total individuals
thermal.df.both.CTmax.50 %>%
  summarise(
    n_species = n_distinct(species),
    total_individuals = n()
  )

thermal.df.both.CTmax.50 %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    n_species = n_distinct(species),
    total_individuals = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )



write.csv(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50_sp, file = "thermal.df.both.CTmax.50_sp.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 2. Number of individuals per species (sorted from highest to lowest)
species_summary_CTmax.50 <- thermal.df.both.CTmax.50 %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(n_individuals = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_individuals))

print(species_summary_CTmax.50)
write.csv(species_summary_CTmax.50, file = "species_summary_CTmax.50.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 3. If you want breakdown by metric and humidity as well:
species_summary_CTmax.50_site<-thermal.df.both.CTmax.50 %>%
  group_by(site, metric, humidity, species) %>%
  summarise(n_individuals = n(), .groups = "drop")

write.csv(species_summary_CTmax.50_site, file = "species_summary_CTmax.50_site.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```




```{r}

lm_site_max50 <- lmer(set_temp.trans~site+(1|species),thermal.df.both.CTmax.50,na.action=na.omit)

overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}

#overdisp_fun
overdisp_fun(lm_site_max50) #p-value is 1.00000000, the model is not overdispered

#pp_check(abundance_best) %>% plot()
model_check_lm_site_max50<-check_model(lm_site_max50)
print(model_check_lm_site_max50)
ggsave("model_check_lm_site_max50.tiff", units="in",width = 16, height = 12,device='tiff', dpi=300)

#Model summaries 
summary(lm_site_max50) # Significant differences in CT max under 50% humidity between sites
Anova(lm_site_max50,test="F")
r.squaredGLMM(lm_site_max50) #R2m=0.4360318   R2c=0.9254454

labels_thermal.df.both.CTmax.50<-thermal.df.both.CTmax.50%>% group_by(site) %>% summarize(mean = mean(set_temp),sd=sd(set_temp))

p_site.all.max<- ggplot(thermal.df.both.CTmax.50, aes(x=site, y=set_temp, fill=site),
                                add = "jitter") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15)+
  geom_boxplot(width=0.4,alpha=0.5) +
  geom_jitter(color="black", size=2, alpha=0.6, position = "jitter")+
  xlab("Species") + 
  ylab("CTmax.50") + # Improve axis labels
  theme_bw(base_size = 35)+
  theme(legend.position = "right")+
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 35),
        text = element_text(size = 35),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 35),
        axis.text.x=element_text(size =30),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size =35),
        axis.title.x=element_text(size =35),
        axis.title.y=element_text(size =40),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 35),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  #remove major-grid labels
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        )+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("subtropics" = "green4",
                               "tropics"="#E69F00"))+
  ylim(32,52)+guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Climate region"))

p_site.all.max
ggsave("p_site.all.max.tiff", units="in",width = 12, height = 9,device='tiff', dpi=600)
```

## New

```{r}

# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) # Required to extract p-values from lmer models
library(ggpubr)

# 1. Filter for 50% humidity and valid species
# We only want species that have BOTH CTmax and CTmin data
thermal_50 <- thermal.df.both.50 %>%
  filter(str_detect(humidity, '50%')) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  filter(any(metric == "CTmax") & any(metric == "CTmin")) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Set up the Monte Carlo Simulation
set.seed(123) # Ensures reproducibility
n_iters <- 1000 # Number of random pairings to simulate
p_values <- numeric(n_iters) # Empty vector to store p-values
simulated_ranges <- list() # To store the datasets for plotting later

# 3. Run the loop
for (i in 1:n_iters) {
  
  # A. Randomly pair CTmax and CTmin within each species
  sim_data <- thermal_50 %>%
    group_by(site, species) %>%
    reframe(
      # To match your actual effort, we generate pairs equal to the minimum 
      # number of CTmax or CTmin observations for that specific species
      n_obs = min(sum(metric == "CTmax"), sum(metric == "CTmin")),
      rand_CTmax = sample(set_temp[metric == "CTmax"], n_obs[1], replace = TRUE),
      rand_CTmin = sample(set_temp[metric == "CTmin"], n_obs[1], replace = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    mutate(range = rand_CTmax - rand_CTmin)
  
  # B. Run the Mixed Model
  # range is predicted by site, controlling for species-level differences
  mod <- lmer(range ~ site + (1|species), data = sim_data)
  
  # C. Extract the p-value for the 'site' effect
  # Row 2 of coefficients is typically the comparison between the two sites
  p_val <- summary(mod)$coefficients[2, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  p_values[i] <- p_val
  
  # Save the first iteration to use for our Main Text plot later
  if (i == 1) { rep_data <- sim_data }
}

# 4. Evaluate the Robustness
# You mentioned significance under 0.005, we will check both 0.05 and 0.005
prop_sig_05 <- mean(p_values < 0.05)
prop_sig_005 <- mean(p_values < 0.005)

cat("Percentage of models with p < 0.05:", prop_sig_05 * 100, "%\n")
cat("Percentage of models with p < 0.005:", prop_sig_005 * 100, "%\n")


# Install the package if you haven't already:
# install.packages("gghalves")
library(gghalves)
library(ggplot2)



p_main <- ggplot(rep_data, aes(x = site, y = range)) +
  # 1. Half-violin on the right
  geom_half_violin(aes(fill = site), side = "r", color = NA, alpha = 0.6, 
                   position = position_nudge(x = 0.1)) +
  
  # 2. Narrow boxplot in the center
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = site), width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA,linewidth = 0.5) +
  
  # 3. Jittered points on the left (FIXED HERE)
  # Convert site to a number and subtract 0.15 to shift it left
  geom_jitter(aes(x = as.numeric(as.factor(site)) - 0.15, color = species), 
              size = 2, alpha = 0.7, width = 0.05,shape = 16) +
  
  # Base theme and labels
  theme_bw(base_size = 35) +
  labs(
    x = "Climate Region", 
    y = expression(Thermal~Breadth~(CT[max] - CT[min])),
    fill = "Climate Region",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("subtropics" = "#00AFBB", "tropics" = "#C3D7A4")) +
  
  # Theme adjustments
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right" 
  )


p_main
ggsave("Main_Text_Thermal_Breadth.tiff", plot = p_main, units = "in", width = 12, height = 9, dpi = 300)


# Convert p-values to a dataframe for plotting
p_df <- data.frame(p_value = p_values)

p_supp <- ggplot(p_df, aes(x = p_value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "gray70", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulated P-values",
    y = "Frequency (out of 1000 iterations)",
    title = "Monte Carlo Resampling P-values"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.06, y = 100, label = "p = 0.05 cutoff", color = "red", hjust = 0)

p_supp
ggsave("Supp_Pvalue_Distribution.tiff", plot = p_supp, units = "in", width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

          main = "Density plot of CTmax-CTmin",
          xlab = "CTmax-CTmin")  # looks normal
ggqqplot(rep_data$range)

hist(rep_data$range, main="Histogram of CTmax-CTmin", xlab="", breaks=10)
skewness(rep_data$range, na.rm = TRUE) # -0.1070671

# use 50% humidity only
```

## Question 2

Question: How do dung beetle thermal tolerances respond under different humidity gradients?

Hypothesis: Increasing humidity will decrease CTmax of dung beetles, because it reduces the ability of the beetles to use evapotranspiration to thermoregulate.

Linear model: CTmax \~ site\*humidity+ (1\|species) We include site because we want to understand if there is an interaction between humidity and site

For this analysis, we only used tropical species, as we were only able to collect enough dung beetle individuals for each experiment from tropical forests. We tested the CTmax and CTmin for dung beetle species under three humidity levels: 30%, 50%, and 90%.

```{r}
overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}
overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}

# Check the normality-CTmax
ggdensity(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp, 
          main = "Density plot of CTmin",
          xlab = "CTmin")  # looks fine
ggqqplot(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp)

hist(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp, main="Histogram of CTmin", xlab="", breaks=10) # looks fine
skewness(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp, na.rm = TRUE) # 0.7305839 positive
shapiro.test(as.numeric(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp))#p=0.0007396 not normal. Will transform

# log transform for moderate positive skewed
thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp.lg<-log10(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp)
shapiro.test(as.numeric(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp.lg))#p= 0.0002025 still not normal



# sqrt transform for moderate positive skewed
thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp.sqrt<-sqrt(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp)
shapiro.test(as.numeric(thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin$set_temp.sqrt))#p= 0.1908 normal


# Without considering the secies and only to see the differences in CTmax when different humidity level applied

lm_ctmin_all<- lmer(set_temp.sqrt~humidity+(1|species),
                 thermal.df.both.trop_CTmin,na.action=na.omit)

plot(lm_ctmin_all)
qqnorm(resid(lm_ctmin_all))
qqline(resid(lm_ctmin_all))
check_heteroscedasticity(lm_ctmin_all) #detected (p = 0.004).

    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}
## For humidity 30%

lm_ctmin.30<-lm(set_temp~species,thermal.df_CTmin.30,na.action=na.omit)
Anova(lm_ctmin.30, test="F") 

overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}
library(lme4)

  mutate(
    length_z = as.numeric(scale(length))
  )


model_length_species <- glm(set_temp ~ humidity * length_z + species,family = gaussian(),data = thermal.df.tropics.traits.CTmax)

overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

#### CTmax new figures

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(ggsignif) 

# 1. Categorize continuous length_z into 3 groups
thermal.df.tropics.traits.CTmax <- thermal.df.tropics.traits.CTmax |>
  mutate(
    body_size_cat = case_when(
      length_z <= -0.5 ~ "Small (−1 SD)",
      length_z > -0.5 & length_z <= 0.5 ~ "Mean",
      length_z > 0.5 ~ "Large (+1 SD)"
    ),
    body_size_cat = factor(body_size_cat, levels = c("Small (−1 SD)", "Mean", "Large (+1 SD)"))
  )

# 2. Build the Plot with Accurate ggsignif Brackets
p_ctmax_body_RH_new <- ggplot(thermal.df.tropics.traits.CTmax, aes(x = body_size_cat, y = set_temp, fill = humidity)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  
  # Violins
  geom_violin(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), scale = "width", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) + 
  
  # Jittered points (aligned inside violins)
  geom_jitter(aes(color = humidity), size = 2, alpha = 0.6, shape = 16, 
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.9)) +
  
  # Mean points
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3, color = "black", 
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
               
  # === SIGNIFICANCE BRACKETS BASED ON EMMEANS CLD ===
  
  # Small (-1 SD): 90%(a), 50%(ab), 30%(b)
  geom_signif(
    y_position = c(48, 48, 49), # Height of brackets
    xmin = c(0.7, 1.0, 0.7),    # Left side (comparing V1-V2, V2-V3, V1-V3)
    xmax = c(1.0, 1.3, 1.3),    # Right side
    annotation = c("ns", "ns", "*"), 
    tip_length = 0.02,
    textsize = 6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  # Mean: 90%(a), 50%(b), 30%(c)
  geom_signif(
    y_position = c(46.5, 46.5, 47.5), 
    xmin = c(1.7, 2.0, 1.7),    
    xmax = c(2.0, 2.3, 2.3),    
    annotation = c("*", "*", "***"), 
    tip_length = 0.02,
    textsize = 6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  # Large (+1 SD): 90%(a), 50%(b), 30%(c)
  geom_signif(
    y_position = c(52, 52, 53), 
    xmin = c(2.7, 3.0, 2.7),    
    xmax = c(3.0, 3.3, 3.3),    
    annotation = c("*", "*", "***"), 
    tip_length = 0.02,
    textsize = 6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # ==================================================
```

```{r}
# 2. Run the EMMeans for the interaction (which you already had)

)

# 3. Extract the Compact Letter Display (CLD) for multiple comparisons
cld_letters <- cld(emm_length2, Letters = letters, adjust = "tukey")
cld_letters <- as.data.frame(cld_letters)

# Clean up the letters (remove extra spaces)
cld_letters$.group <- trimws(cld_letters$.group)

# Format the body_size column in the letters dataframe to exactly match the plot
cld_letters$body_size_cat <- factor(cld_letters$length_z,
  levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
  labels = c("Small (−1 SD)", "Mean", "Large (+1 SD)")
)

# 4. Set a Y-axis position for where the letters should float above the violins
# We will place them slightly above the maximum CTmax value
y_max <- max(thermal.df.tropics.traits.CTmax$set_temp, na.rm = TRUE)
cld_letters$y_pos <- y_max + 0.8
```

```{r}
overdisp_fun <- overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
    rdf <- df.residual(model)
    rp <- residuals(model,type="pearson")
    Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
    prat <- Pearson.chisq/rdf
    pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df=rdf, lower.tail=FALSE)
    c(chisq=Pearson.chisq,ratio=prat,rdf=rdf,p=pval)
}
```

```{r}
    annotation = c("*", "*", "***"),

    color = "black"
  ) +

  geom_signif(
    y_position = c(10.5, 10.5, 12), 
    xmin = c(2.7, 3.0, 2.7),    
    xmax = c(3.0, 3.3, 3.3),    
    annotation = c("*", "*", "***"), 
    tip_length = 0.02,
    textsize = 6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # ==================================================

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#0072B2")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#0072B2")) + 
  
  labs(x = "Body Size Category", y = "CTmin", fill = "Humidity", color = "Humidity") + 
  theme_bw(base_size = 35) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.background = element_blank(),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 35),
```

# Multiple Factor Analysis (MFA) for trait data

Reference- <http://www.sthda.com/english/articles/31-principal-component-methods-in-r-practical-guide/116-mfa-multiple-factor-analysis-in-r-essentials/>

We employ variables encompassing soil chemical and physical properties, forest structure, topographical features, and climate conditions in this context. These variables collectively characterize the distinct habitats present across various sites.

The environmental variables have can organize in to several categories

```         
1)First group - Site information (first 6 columns)
1)Second group- Soil chemical properties, continuous variables, next 4 columns
2)Third group - Soil physical properties next 4 columns
3)Fourth group- Vegetation structure next 2 columns
4)Fifth group- Site slope next 1 columns
5)Sixth group- Site direction next 1 columns
```

“c” or “s” for quantitative variables. If “s”, the variables are scaled to unit variance. “n” for categorical variables. “f” for frequencies (from a contingency tables).

```{r}
#libraries
library("FactoMineR")
library("factoextra")

# Data arranging

e.data.MFA<-read.csv("community_and_e_data/alpha_e_data.csv")
thermal.df.MFA <- thermal.df[ -c(1:2,5:8) ] # isolate the trait data

colnames(e.data.MFA)

str(e.data.MFA)

group = c(1,4,4,4,2,3,3,3)
name.group = c("site", # Describes the site
               "community",
               "chemical", # Describes the soil chemical properties
               "physical", # Describes the soil physical properties
               "vegetation", # Describes the vegetation structure
               #"slope_aspect", # Describes the topography
               "temperature", # Describes  temperature
               "light", # Describes the dry season light availability
               "beta" # Components of the beta diversity
                        ) 

e.data.mfa <- MFA(e.data.MFA, 
               group = c(1,4,4,4,2,3,3,3), 
               type = c("n","s","s","s","s","s","s","s"),
               name.group=c("site","community","chemical","physical","vegetation","temperature", "light","beta"),
               num.group.sup = c(1,2,8),
               graph = TRUE)

print(e.data.mfa)
e.data.mfa.eig.val <- get_eigenvalue(e.data.mfa)
head(e.data.mfa.eig.val)

p_eig_screen_plot<-fviz_screeplot(e.data.mfa)+
  theme(legend.position = "right")+
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 35),
        text = element_text(size = 40),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 35),
        axis.text.x=element_text(size =30),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size =35),
        axis.title.x=element_text(size =35),
        axis.title.y=element_text(size =40),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 35))

print(p_eig_screen_plot)
ggsave("p_eig_screen_plot.tiff", units="in",width = 12, height = 9,device='tiff', dpi=300)

# Coordinates of groups
#head(group$coord)
# Cos2: quality of representation on the factor map
#head(group$cos2)
# Contributions to the  dimensions
#head(group$contrib)

quanti.var <- get_mfa_var(e.data.mfa, "quanti.var")
quanti.var 

# Coordinates
head(quanti.var$coord)
```
